title: MongoDB Transactions
summary: Group document writes, then configure and apply their transaction boundary.

sources.title: Spring Data MongoDB: sessions and transactions

richText: A transaction groups database operations so they commit together or roll back together.
Commit makes the transaction changes permanent. Rollback discards its uncommitted changes.
MongoDB already makes a single-document write atomic. Use a multi-document transaction when several writes must succeed together.
Multi-document transactions require a replica set or a supported sharded cluster. A standalone MongoDB server is not enough.
A replica set is a MongoDB deployment whose servers maintain copies of the same data.
MongoTransactionManager starts and manages MongoDB transactions through MongoDatabaseFactory.
@Transactional does not supply this manager by itself. Register a MongoTransactionManager bean.
The manager and participating MongoDB operations must use the same database factory.

example.title: Register the MongoDB transaction manager
description: Use the MongoDB starter and a URI for a replica-set or supported sharded deployment.
Place this configuration under the application package.
explanation: The bean uses the MongoDatabaseFactory configured for the application.
Its bean name is mongoTransactionManager. A service can select that name explicitly.

richText: Put the boundary on a service
@Transactional marks the operations that should run in one transaction.
In the default proxy-based setup, another bean must call the service method through the Spring-managed object.
A call from one method to another method on the same instance bypasses that proxy. The called method annotation does not start a new transaction.
By default, RuntimeException and Error cause rollback. Use rollbackFor when a checked exception must cause rollback.
If code catches a failure and returns normally, the transaction can commit. Let failures reach the transaction boundary when rollback is required.
A database transaction cannot undo an email or external HTTP request.

example.title: Save an entry and reference in one transaction
description: Use JournalEntryRepository, UserRepository and User from the earlier MongoDB pages.
The user must already exist. Pass a new JournalEntry and its owner ID.
Call createEntry through the injected JournalService bean.
explanation: The service explicitly selects the MongoDB transaction manager.
It loads the user, saves the entry and saves the reference in the same transaction.
If a participating save fails with a runtime exception, the transaction rolls back its database writes.
This boundary groups writes. It does not by itself prevent every concurrent update conflict.
